steps.title: The confusing note
paragraphs: On Monday, Zoe’s cousin called and said, “I’ll visit tomorrow.”
On Friday, Zoe told her dad, “Lila said she would visit tomorrow.”
“No,” said Zoe. “She meant Tuesday. She’s already been!”
Words like tomorrow, here and now depend on when and where they were said. When you report them later, they have to change.

cards.title: Time words
cards.text:
now → then · today → that day · tonight → that night
tomorrow → the next day / the following day
yesterday → the day before / the previous day
next week → the following week · last week → the week before
this morning → that morning · two days ago → two days before
cards.note: The new words point back to the day the words were spoken, not to today.

cards.title: Place and pointing words
cards.text: here → there · this → that · these → those
cards.note: “I left my bag here” said in the gym → She said she had left her bag there.

cards.title: Putting it all together
cards.text:
Coach (on Monday): “We will practise here tomorrow.”
Reported (on Friday): Coach said that we would practise there the next day.
cards.note: Pronoun ✓ (we stays: you were on the team) · verb ✓ (will → would) · place ✓ (here → there) · time ✓ (tomorrow → the next day).

cards.title: Same day, same place?
cards.body: If you report the words on the same day and in the same place, you can keep them: at lunch, “Mom said she’s picking us up here today.” Shift them when the time or place has changed.

prompts: Which time word did you change in your message? What would go wrong if you hadn’t?
Make a list of the four changes to check in reported speech (pronouns, verbs, time, place). Which do you forget most?
